comments.content: The new glob-to-regex conversion `(\/?)\*` -> `($1.*)?` makes the trailing `*` optional, which changes semantics. For a rule like `/path/to/dir/*`, the regex becomes `^/path/to/dir/(/.*)?$`. This matches `/path/to/dir/` (with trailing slash) but not `/path/to/dir` (without trailing slash). Since `ensureLeadingAndTrailingSlash` is applied to the input path in `isEnabled`, this may be fine for that call site, but `Override.asRegex()` is also used in `isChildOf` where `this.baseRule` (which always has a trailing slash) is tested. Verify that the optional group is intentional and that all call sites pass paths with trailing slashes; otherwise, rules like `/path/to/dir/*` will fail to match `/path/to/dir`.

`isChildOf` uses `parent.asRegex().test(this.baseRule)`. Because `asRegex` for a parent with `includeSubdirs=true` produces a regex that requires a trailing slash (e.g. `^/path/to/dir/(/.*)?$`), and `this.baseRule` is normalized to end with `/`, this works. However, if the parent rule is `/` (root), `asRegex` becomes `^(/.*)?$` which matches everything — that's likely intended. But note that `isChildOf` returns true for the parent itself when the child equals the parent (since `baseRule` matches). Combined with the `isEqualTo` check in `enable`/`disable`, this is handled, but callers should be aware.

The `handleDisable` function silently falls back to `SettingScope.User` for any scope value that isn't `'workspace'` (case-insensitive). While the `.check()` validates the scope, this fallback is fragile: if a new scope is added to `SettingScope` in the future, it will be silently treated as `User`. Consider explicitly handling each valid scope or throwing on unknown values to avoid silent misbehavior.

Same issue as `disable.ts`: `handleEnable` silently defaults to `SettingScope.User` for any non-`workspace` scope. The docstring for the `--scope` option says "If not set, will be enabled in all scopes", but the implementation only enables in `User` scope when scope is unset. This is a behavior/documentation mismatch — either update the description or implement the documented behavior.

In `enable`, the filter removes rules where `fileOverride.isChildOf(override)` is true. But `isChildOf` returns `false` when `parent.includeSubdirs` is false. So when enabling a parent without subdirs (e.g. `/path/to/dir` with `includeSubdirs=false`), child rules like `/path/to/dir/subdir1/` are NOT removed. This is tested in `'should not remove child rules if includeSubdirs is false'`, so it appears intentional. However, this creates a subtle inconsistency: a non-subdir parent rule `/path/to/dir/` will not match `/path/to/dir/subdir1` (since the regex requires exact match), so the child rule still applies — which is correct. Just confirming the intent is documented.

`disable` now delegates to `enable` with a `!`-prefixed path. This is clever, but `Override.fromInput` strips the leading `!` and sets `isDisable=true`, then `output()` re-adds it. The `conflictsWith` logic compares `isDisable`, so a disable rule will correctly conflict with an enable rule at the same path. However, `isChildOf` does not consider `isDisable` — so disabling a parent will remove child enable rules (as tested). Verify this is the desired semantics: disabling `/path/to/dir` with subdirs removes an explicit enable for `/path/to/dir/subdir1`, which seems correct since the parent disable covers it.

The test was changed from `manager.disable('ext-test', true, '*')` to `manager.disable('ext-test', true, '/')`. With the new `ensureLeadingAndTrailingSlash`, `'*'` would become `'/*/'` which is likely not intended. Using `'/'` is more correct, but note that `Override.fromInput('/', true)` produces `baseRule='/'` and `output()` returns `'/*'`. The regex for `'/*'` is `^(/.*)?$` which matches everything — good. Just confirming the test change is intentional and not masking a regression in handling `'*'` as a global disable.
The test name `'should handle'` is not descriptive. Consider renaming to something like `'should allow a more specific disable rule to override a parent enable rule'` to clarify intent.
